verdicts.message: High: watchdog-assembled-code-string-evaluated-ts: This call evaluates a code string that was ASSEMBLED at runtime -- a value is spliced into JavaScript source the author wrote around it, and the result is handed to `eval`/`new Function` to be executed. The surrounding syntax is the author's, so a value carrying `)`, `;` or a newline does not stay in the expression slot it was written for: it closes that slot and continues as statements, with the full authority of this module. Because the splice happens behind a reusable function, every caller inherits that authority without being told. Parse or validate the value instead of executing it -- `JSON.parse` for data, a purpose-built expression evaluator for expressions -- or bind it as an ARGUMENT, `new Function('value', body)` invoked with the value, so it can never be read as code.
verdicts.reason: True: the custom YAML tag compiles a scalar from the uploaded layout with new Function. It is the planted DESER-001 defect seen as code injection; the key labels the site insecure-deserialization (README, Contested truths).

verdicts.message: Medium: watchdog-open-redirect-default-operand-js: This redirect sends the user wherever the REQUEST says to go, and the `|| '/'` default in front of it is not the guard it looks like. A default chooses what happens when the parameter is ABSENT; it never constrains what happens when the parameter is HOSTILE. Whenever the caller supplies any value at all the left operand wins, so the caller picks the destination, and `?? '/'` behaves the same way -- it only widens "absent" from falsy to null-or-undefined. The browser follows it, so this endpoint sends its own users wherever the caller says: a redirect that starts on your domain, in your TLS certificate and next to your brand, and lands on a page the caller wrote. That first hop is the whole value of an open redirect, which is why they are the standard carrier for phishing, for OAuth `redirect_uri` theft, and for slipping past allow-lists that only inspect the host a user clicked. "Send them back where they came from, else home" needs a destination this code controls: keep an explicit allow-list and test membership before redirecting (`if (!ALLOWED.includes(dest)) return res.redirect('/')`), or accept a same-origin path only and require a single leading `/` (`/^\/(?!\/)/`) so a scheme-relative `//host` cannot pass. Where an absolute URL is genuinely needed, resolve it against a fixed base -- `new URL(dest, 'https://your.host/')` -- and let the base own the origin.

verdicts.message: Changelog looks stale/thin: The changelog this check read carries 2 versioned entries, against a bar of 3. Counted as either an `x.y.z` string or a version-shaped section heading (`## [1.2.0]`, `## V14.x.x`, `## Updates in 8.0.x`), whichever is the larger — so a log sectioned by minor series counts its sections, not its individual patch numbers. Entries recorded somewhere this check does not read — release notes generated at tag time from a generator config it did not recognise, or a log kept outside the repository — are not counted here, and this row is about what is re-findable in the tree rather than about how often you release.

verdicts.message: Duplication concentrated across 8 sibling directories (6 clone groups): 6 duplicated blocks under src/ have copies in at least two of the sibling directories conversion, exports, feeds, imports, saved-searches, search (+2 more sibling(s) not listed) — 3 of them are reported below, and 3 are counted here but not reported individually: those copies match on shape but no longer clear R10's bar for an individually reported row — either they kept neither their own names nor their values, or what was copied is too small to stand on its own (it reports near-exact duplication only, and only of substantial extent). What this row states is the concentration, which the detector measured over all 6 and which does not depend on how exactly each block's copies still match. That concentration is one structural fact, not 6 local ones: the siblings replicate behaviour none of them owns, which is the shape of a missing shared module — a common library every sibling imports — rather than 6 separate extractions. Check first whether the siblings are deliberately standalone deliverables (scaffold templates, demo apps that must stay copy-pasteable); where they are, the duplication is the design and the per-block rows are the ones to act on.

verdicts.message: Duplicated block (15 lines × 2 locations): src/imports/import-routes.ts:47 · src/imports/import-routes.ts:68 — all 2 copies are in the same file, and the CITED SPAN is not a self-contained block — it runs from inside one construct into the next (the tail of a branch plus the head of the following one, a run of switch arms, the end of a declaration plus the list that follows it) rather than covering a whole unit. So do not lift these lines literally: no call can be substituted for a half-open construct. verdicts.message: Weak hash algorithm: MD5/SHA1 is computed here, and both are collision-broken. If this digest protects anything — a signature, an integrity or tamper check, a credential, or any value an attacker can influence — that is a real weakness: use SHA-256+ (`createHash("sha256")`) for content integrity, or a KDF (bcrypt/Argon2/scrypt) for password storage. If it only derives a non-security identifier (a cache key, an avatar URL, an ETag), collision resistance carries no security consequence here; make that intent explicit instead — a non-cryptographic hash such as xxhash or murmurhash says it in code — since the algorithm alone cannot distinguish the two uses. Where a protocol this code does not own fixes the digest (a k-anonymity range query, a legacy signature format), the protocol decides; say so beside the call. This repository constructs a collision-broken hash (MD5/SHA1) at 2 sites, not one: `src/documents/etag.ts:8` (createHash("md5")), `src/shares/share-password.ts:5` (createHash("md5")). Each is a separate decision — fixing only the line this row cites leaves the others in place.

Ensure the 'Contributing' section in the README contains clear instructions for new contributors.
verdicts.reason: Disproof: README.md:64-68 '## Contributing' says to open an issue before larger work, that PRs target main and must pass CI (formatting, lint, type-check, build, tests with coverage thresholds), to add tests with every behaviour change, record ADRs and note changes in CHANGELOG.md.

verdicts.message: The ADR lacks a clear problem statement or motivation explaining why these specific constraints are necessary (e.g., security risks, performance issues, or compliance requirements).: Add a 'Problem' or 'Motivation' section before 'Context' that explicitly states the risks or issues this decision addresses, such as preventing SSRF attacks, ensuring data privacy, or managing latency.
verdicts.reason: Accurate: docs/adr/0003-outbound-requests.md lists the four outbound request kinds (Context) and the constraints (Decision) but never says why they are constrained (server-side request forgery, data exposure, slow hosts). Minor documentation gap; uncertain resolves to valid, consistent with the D20 'valid' verdicts on bench-csharp-readiness and bench-csharp-blazor-a11y.
verdicts.action: valid, found after freeze - candidate for next key version. Repository NOT changed (frozen at v1.0.0).

verdicts.message: Split (repository root): The project contains 153 public types spread across 18 distinct namespaces that represent unrelated functional domains (such as reports, subscriptions, search, imports, and documents) rather than layers of a single responsibility. Suggested: Split into separate projects for `src/reports`, `src/subscriptions`, `src/http`, `src/exports`, `src/search`, `src/imports`, `src/saved-searches`, `web/src`, `src/documents`, `src/shares`, `src/feeds`, `src/conversion`, `src/preferences`, and `src/templates`.
verdicts.reason: Counts are accurate (one package, ~150 public types, feature folders); the call to split a single small service organised by feature folders (ADR 0001) into separate projects is not supported by the measurement. Same judgement as the contained D26 row of iteration 1.

falseNegatives.reason: Search term interpolated into a quoted ILIKE literal of a node-postgres query (template literal passed to pool.query inside a repository method). No baked rule models node-postgres query text built from a method parameter; the taint rules need the request object in the same function.
Owner interpolated into a knex raw() template. node-knex-sqli did not fire: the value arrives as a repository parameter, not from req in the same function.
Unvalidated req.body fields used as a MongoDB deleteOne filter (operator injection). No baked rule for MongoDB filters built from a request body (the only CWE-943 rules are DynamoDB/AWS Lambda).
Caller-chosen format spliced into a command line run by child_process.exec. detect-child-process only taints request values in the same function; here the value is a method parameter.

path.join(root, id, req.params.name) then readFile in an Express handler. The request-param-to-fs-read rule runs with taint_assume_safe_functions, so path.join drops the taint; express-path-join-resolve-traversal did not fire either.
libxmljs2 parseXml with noent: true on an uploaded document. express-libxml-noent needs the request in the same expression; the parse sits in a reader function called with a string.

YAML schema extended with a !!js/function tag that compiles the scalar, used to load uploaded layouts. No rule for js-yaml custom types; the scanner reported the new Function inside the tag as code injection (valid, counted as code-injection noise by the harness).
vm.runInNewContext on a caller's formula. The vm-injection rules need the request in the same function.

Recursive merge of req.body into stored preferences copies __proto__. The only CWE-1321 rule (prototype-lookup-request-key-js) needs req.body as the bracket key inside the handler; the merge is a generic function.

res.redirect(303, next) where next is req.query.next when it is a string. The open-redirect rules source only req.get/req.header (request-accessor) or a default operand; a ternary over req.query is not modelled.
new RegExp(pattern) on a caller-supplied pattern run over document text. No baked JS rule for dynamic RegExp construction.
Caller-chosen file name written into a plain-text audit line with appendFile. The only log-injection rule is Java's crlf-injection-logs.
Share-link passwords stored as unsalted MD5 (createHash('md5').update(password)). S1's weak-hash arm fired on the MD5 ETag trap but not here, and no password-hash/KDF row was raised for TypeScript.
Subscriber e-mail address logged as a field of a pino record (logger.info({ email: subscription.email }, ...)). The personal-data-in-log rule did not match the object-literal field form.
Recipient e-mail addresses stored in localStorage. personal-data-in-browser-storage did not fire: the stored value is a JSON array of addresses under a key without a personal-data name.

scoreBands.note: No model-judged bands in this repository, so no --with-llm pass was run. S1 scored 80 in all three iterations; it does not assess server controls for TypeScript and its weak-hash arm missed the MD5 password store, so the band (web-security posture, set before the first scan) is kept and the miss recorded.

observations: Recall 6/21 (28.6%). The hits are rules that see request data and the sink in one handler (SSRF from req.query to fetch, raw HTML format, personal data in a URL) plus the structural X-cards (X17 uncapped recursion, X24 document value into innerHTML) and one syntactic rule (assembled code string into new Function). Every miss is a sink reached through a function parameter (repositories, converters, readers, merge helpers) or a construct no baked rule models for JS/TS: node-postgres/knex text, MongoDB filters, vm, js-yaml custom types, dynamic RegExp, plain-text log lines, localStorage.

Trap resistance 20/25. Caught: TRP-011 (new Function over a fixed field table), TRP-015 (redirect behind a same-site path validator read as a default operand), TRP-018 (MD5 ETag), TRP-022 (email=true flag, as in C#), TRP-025 (named scopes, as in the TS baseline).

D8 measured 44% line coverage against the suite's 96.8%: the scanner installs with npm ci --ignore-scripts, so a dependency with a native binding fetched at install time (libxmljs2) cannot load and every suite that imports the app fails. Engine fact for the owner: coverage of any repository with such a dependency is misreported.

res-render-injection (registry rule) fires on any `.render(` call with request data in scope — three service methods named render here; R6 read `new URL('../../views/', import.meta.url)` as an unresolvable import.

Harness: the DESER-001 site was reported as code-injection and counted as noise; a deserialization/code-injection family (or a multi-concept entry) would let a scanner that names the code-execution consequence score the plant. New concepts nosql-injection and prototype-pollution were added for this repository (scanner-benchmark f933b50).
Repository fixes from valid findings: route duplication (helpers), reportRoutes and validateNode complexity, a silent localStorage fallback, and no accessibility check (axe-core added).

Final host pass (TS sidecar repaired): model rows add 8 M4 false positives (files and directories the README names do exist), a D19 false positive (the Contributing section exists), a D26 split opinion, and one D20 row judged valid: ADR 0003 states no motivation for its outbound-request constraints. That is recorded as valid, found after freeze - candidate for next key version; the frozen repository is not changed.
